step: 6.2.5c player application volume and quiet media UI
status: implemented; automated/native checks passed; user reported successful tests
user_scope: Only the media player's application volume, explicitly not Windows master volume
ownership: Media -> media.control -> registry/policy/TaskManager; dashboard and REST/Live share action set_volume

implementation.adapter: app/tools/local/media_volume.py; fixed Windows Core Audio interfaces through ctypes; no new dependency
implementation.scope: one unambiguously matched active application audio session, or one inactive match if none active
implementation.identity: exact GSMTC source to process app ID/executable name/stem; private endpoint/session-instance/PID target
implementation.volume: absolute finite 0-100; readback tolerance 0.1 percentage points; existing mute is preserved
implementation.ui: theme-bound range commits on change, never on every input event; operation status is off-screen aria-live, not visible text
implementation.excluded: endpoint/master volume, keyboard volume, Vex reply/effects volume, mute writes and arbitrary PID/session selection

covered: exact identity matching and real ambiguity refusal; active versus old inactive selection
zero, invalid percentage, missing source, unsupported sessions and preserved mute
stale audio target, device/session changes, Stop before dispatch and late Stop after verified change
unknown write/readback/metadata-loss outcomes and persistent core locking after restart
real REST/Live SDK with synthetic transport through the same tools; repeated call ID writes only once
UI input preview versus committed change, capability/chat locks, correct action/target/percent
saved theme follows the range while reactor state changes do not recolor it
native WebView2 range -> bridge -> actual core -> synthetic application volume; hidden operation status
initial_failures_and_corrections: First test collection omitted the parametrized mode argument; fixture signature corrected.

First browser color assertion tried to read a Chromium native slider pseudo-element and received the input background. Verification now observes real theme changes and stability across reactor states; visual preview also reviewed.
Initial type inference rejected unpacking the adapter result. The adapter now declares its dictionary return contract; final type checking passed.
Real read-only mapping initially included stale inactive browser sessions as competing targets. Explicit active-session preference was added and tested; multiple active matches remain refused.
Review found that metadata failure after a volume write could lose dispatch knowledge. Shared native dispatch tracking now preserves unknown, with a dedicated regression.

First standalone preview import used a Windows path instead of an ESM file URL, then an early screenshot caught the entry animation before visibility. Import fixed and preview recaptured after the entry animation.
limits: Browser volume is application audio, not a single tab. Multiple applicable sessions, unmapped IDs, denied access or exclusive-mode streams may disable volume control.
No fallback to system volume or another application; existing per-application mute is not cleared.
Native Core Audio calls are synchronous. A surrounding timeout does not prove the underlying call was cancelled; unknown stays locked without automatic retry.
Earlier same-title playback, persistent reconciliation, pythonnet teardown and native-smoke type-complexity boundaries remain open.

No real application volume writes, paid API requests or user-data mutations were performed. User reported successful tests; specific provider/hardware coverage was not enumerated. Portable EXE was not rebuilt.
manual_test: Restart source app, play media, move PLAYER VOLUME and compare only that application in Windows Volume Mixer. Ask Vex to set player volume to 30%. Check system and Vex reply-volume preferences remain unchanged.
commit: Accepted work committed under AGENTS.md; no push requested
manual_acceptance: User accepted this step; specific actual-provider/hardware coverage was not enumerated.
